Poverty reduction is especially difficult in economies affected by conflict and institutional weakness, which typically face compounding challenges even after the conflict has subsided (Corral et al. 2020; Federle et al. 2024; Korn and Stemmler 2025; Novta and Pugacheva 2021; World Bank 2025b). Conflict destroys assets and disrupts livelihoods, whereas poverty fuels grievances and weakens the capacity of the state to prevent violence (Corral et al. 2020).

These challenges are compounded by the current global environment, in which economies dependent on energy imports and economies directly affected by conflict face the weakest growth prospects (World Bank 2026c). Furthermore, when a population grows quickly, the economy must expand even more quickly to deliver the same level of improvement in per capita welfare.

context_candidates.text: To investigate the disproportionate impact, two methods allow variation in the intensity of the shock faced by households (Kimura et al. 2026). In both cases, the average growth of the economy is maintained at the level indicated in Global Economic Prospects, June 2026 (World Bank 2026c), which captures the aggregate income and price shock. First, households are allocated sectoral growth rates based on their sector of employment. Second, inflation is allocated to households depending on their budget’s exposure to food and energy. Poorer households typically spend a greater share on food and energy and thus receive lower real income if the prices of these items rise. A distribution-neutral assumption, which is used as the baseline throughout the report, would instead assume the equal distribution of inflationary shocks.

metadata.section: Gains in global poverty reduction could be reversed in coming decades

context_candidates.text: Allowing for distributional impacts either from uneven income shocks or price shocks leads to a further increase compared with the preconflict projections and essentially a stagnation in extreme poverty relative to 2025 (when the number was 816.9 million people). Taking the differential impact of sectoral growth rates into consideration reveals that 816.6 million people were estimated to be living in extreme poverty in 2026. One of the main reasons is that projected agricultural growth is much lower than the growth projected in the service and industrial sectors in 2026. Because a larger share of the extreme poor work in the agricultural sector, poverty reduction is muted because of the low agricultural growth. This also highlights that it is important for the poor to engage in resilient high-growth sectors to favor poverty reduction (refer to chapter 4).

results.text: To investigate the disproportionate impact, two methods allow variation in the intensity of the shock faced by households (Kimura et al. 2026). In both cases, the average growth of the economy is maintained at the level indicated in Global Economic Prospects, June 2026 (World Bank 2026c), which captures the aggregate income and price shock. A distribution-neutral assumption, which is used as the baseline throughout the report, would instead assume the equal distribution of inflationary shocks.

Nói cách khác, cơ sở này giả định mức tăng trưởng thu nhập trung bình được áp dụng như nhau cho các hộ, không làm thay đổi bất bình đẳng. Ngược lại, kịch bản sốc thu nhập và sốc giá có điều chỉnh phân phối: ở kịch bản sốc giá, tăng trưởng thực tế của hộ được điều chỉnh theo mức chi tiêu thực phẩm và năng lượng, giảm với hộ có mức phơi nhiễm trên trung bình và tăng với các hộ còn lại để khớp với tăng trưởng trung bình của kịch bản cơ sở. Lưu ý: đoạn nguồn bị cắt ngang ở phần mô tả cách tính tăng trưởng thu nhab trung bình trong kịch bản sốc thu nhập, nên không có chi tiết công thức đầy đủ cho kịch bản đó.
